cases.question: Summarize concrete mix
cases.answer:
I found more than one matching section. Which one do you mean?
• Specification 03300, section 2.05, CONCRETE MIX (page 17)
• Specification 03310, section 2.02, CONCRETE MIX (page 60)

cases.question: Summarize section 2.05 concrete mix in specification 03300
cases.answer:
*   A minimum of 5.75 bags of cement per cubic yard of concrete must be used [Page 17].
*   Concrete must achieve a compressive strength of 2400 psi at 7 days and 4000 psi at 28 days [Page 17].
*   Slump should be 3 to 4 inches for concrete cast against earth in slabs and footings and where used as a topping, and 5 to 6 inches for concrete in supported slabs, beams, columns, and walls [Page 17].
*   The maximum water/cement ratio shall be 0.50 [Page 17].
*   Air entraining agent should be added to normal weight concrete mixes for work exposed to temperatures lower than 40 degrees F, with a maximum air content of 3 percent for concrete with trowel finished surfaces and 3-5 percent for other concrete [Page 17].

cases.question: Summarize section 2.02 concrete mix in specification 03310
cases.answer:
Key exact values:
E. Water-Cement Ratios:
1. Maximum allowable water-cement ratios shall be as follows:
a. Concrete for liquid-containing structures: 0.45.
b. Concrete subjected to brackish water, salt spray or deicers: 0.40.
c. All other concrete: 0.55. [Page 62]

*   The objective is to select ingredient proportions to achieve proper placability, durability, strength, appearance, and other specified properties [Page 60].
*   Mix designs must be prepared by an independent commercial testing laboratory acceptable to the Owner [Page 60].
*   Compressive strength is determined by testing 6-inch diameter by 12-inch high cylinders in accordance with ASTM C192 and ASTM C39, with an average compressive strength of at least 125 percent of the specified strength at 28 days [Page 61].
*   Slump tests are performed to monitor uniformity and consistency of concrete delivered to the job site, but these tests should not be the basis for mix design [Page 62].
*   Maximum allowable water-cement ratios are specified [Page 61].
*   Air content in concrete should be 4 to 6 percent, except for drilled shafts [Page 62].
*   Water quantity must be sufficient to allow proper workability without segregation and compaction by vibratory methods [Page 62].

cases.question: What is the maximum water cement ratio in section 2.05 of specification 03300
What compressive strengths and slump ranges are specified in section 2.05 of specification 03300
cases.answer:
*   Compressive Strength at 7 days is 2400 psi [Page 17].
*   Compressive Strength at 28 days is 4000 psi [Page 17].
*   Slump ranges are 3 to 4 inches for concrete cast against earth in slabs and footings and where used as a topping, and 5 to 6 inches for concrete in supported slabs, beams, columns and walls [Page 17].

cases.question: When may accelerating and set retarding admixtures be used in section 2.05 of specification 03300
cases.answer: Accelerating admixtures may be used in cold weather only when approved by the Engineer [Page 17]. Set retarding admixtures should be used during hot weather only when approved by the Engineer [Page 17].

cases.question: Summarize section 3.26 curing in specification 03300
cases.answer:
*   Curing for Type II or IP cement requires preventing moisture loss, rapid temperature change, and mechanical injury for 7 curing days, and for Type III cement, it requires 3 curing days [Page 44].
*   Start curing as soon as free water has disappeared from the concrete surface after placing and finishing [Page 44].
*   A curing day is defined as any calendar day when the temperature is above 50 degrees F for at least 19 hours, or if the adjacent air temperature is maintained above 50 degrees F in continued cold weather [Page 44].
*   For surfaces not requiring a rubbed finish, forms should remain in place for the full curing period, and wood forms must be kept wet during curing [Page 44].
*   For unformed surfaces, cure should be done by the membrane curing compound method, which involves immediately sealing the surface with a uniform coating of approved curing compound after surplus water sheen disappears [Page 45].
*   For rubbed finishes, forms should be removed as soon as practicable without damaging the surface, followed by continuing curing with approved compounds or moist cotton mats until the normal curing period is complete [Page 45].

cases.question: What minimum solids content and color requirement apply to membrane forming curing compound in specification 03300
cases.answer:
*   The minimum solids content for a membrane-forming curing compound is 30 percent [Page 24].
*   When used for liquid-containing structures, the curing compound must be white-pigmented [Page 24].

cases.question: What are the minimum and maximum slump values for Portland cement concrete and concrete dosed with superplasticizer
cases.answer:
- Portland Cement Concrete: minimum 2”; maximum 4” [Page 62]
- Concrete to be dosed with superplasticizer: minimum 1”; maximum 3” [Page 62]

cases.question: Which concrete class has 5000 psi compressive strength and 658 pounds of cement per cubic yard
What standard and class must plywood form material meet
cases.answer: Plywood form material must conform to PS 1, Class 1 [Page 17].

cases.question: List the maximum water cement ratios in specification 03310
cases.answer:

cases.question: What color must structural steel handrails be painted
cases.answer: The document does not contain information about the required color for structural steel handrails.

cases.question: What is the minimum curing period for mass concrete in specification 03300
cases.answer: The minimum curing period for mass concrete is 2 weeks [Page 45].

cases.question: What about when ambient temperature is below freezing
cases.answer: When ambient air temperature falls below 32 degrees F, protect surface of concrete against freezing. [Page 45]

cases.question: The surveying team is checking the formwork for the new piers. What is the maximum allowable variation from plumb?
cases.answer: Variation In Maximum From Plumb of Specified Surfaces of columns, piers and walls — 1/2" in 10’ [Page 49]

cases.question: Got it. What about the cross-sectional dimensions? How much tolerance do we have on the column thickness?
cases.answer: Drawing Dimensions — Cross section of columns, caps, walls, beams, and similar members — ±1/2”, -1/4” [Page 49]

cases.question: Okay, and what is the tolerance for the level of the top surfaces of the curbs?
cases.answer: The tolerance for the top surfaces of curbs and railings is 3/16" in 10' [Page 49][Page 12]. The drawing dimensions for the cross section of columns, caps, walls, beams, and similar members are ±1/2", -1/4" [Page 49][Page 12].
